headline: Oil fell 2% to about $98 a barrel
commentary: Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell 2.0% to $98.30 a barrel. Oil can reach households through gasoline, freight, airfare, and petroleum-based materials. One morning does not establish a trend.

defines.used_by_and_why: Used to price contracts and plan fuel costs.

explains.anchor_text: reach households through gasoline, freight, airfare, and petroleum-based materials
explains.why: Crude becomes fuel and materials used in transportation and production.
explains.other_reading: Refining, taxes, inventories, contracts, and competition affect retail prices.

visual.title: Oil reaches household costs
visual.caption: Crude feeds fuel, freight, and petroleum-based materials.
visual.alt: Brent crude at 98 dollars and 30 cents per barrel passes through fuel, materials, transportation, and production before reaching household prices.

views.body: Fuel prices can respond before grocery and delivery prices. Long commutes and frequent flights increase exposure to oil changes.
views.keep_wondering: Will the decline last long enough to reach retail prices?

views.body: Oil affects costs for airlines, shippers, farms, and manufacturers. Demand and competition influence whether companies change prices or margins.
views.keep_wondering: Which industries pass lower energy costs to customers first?

views.body: Oil importers can spend less abroad when crude falls. Exporters can receive less revenue. Currencies and shipping routes alter each country's result.
views.keep_wondering: Which importers benefit most from lower oil?

data_note: Intraday oil prices can change quickly. Retail fuel prices vary by time and region.

headline: Government borrowing rates dipped to 5.25%
commentary: The 10-year Treasury yield is the annual return investors demand to lend to the U.S. government for a decade. It dipped from 5.31% to 5.25%. The benchmark can influence mortgages, company expansion, and stock prices relative to profits.

defines.definition: Annual return demanded on a ten-year U.S. government loan.
defines.used_by_and_why: Reference for mortgages, business debt, and long-term borrowing.

explains.anchor_text: influence mortgages, company expansion, and stock prices relative to profits
explains.why: Lenders and investors compare other opportunities with Treasury returns, then adjust for risk.
explains.other_reading: Competition, borrower quality, and earnings can outweigh the benchmark.

visual.title: The 10-year reaches everyday borrowing
visual.source: Federal Reserve via FRED and The Associated Press
visual.caption: Treasury returns provide a reference for other borrowing costs.
visual.alt: A 5.25 percent 10-year Treasury yield branches to mortgages, business loans, and stock prices relative to profits.

views.body: Borrowing costs affect companies refinancing debt or funding expansion. Firms with cash or fixed-rate debt depend less on new loans.
Federal Reserve officials compare inflation and employment with borrowing conditions. Treasury issuance can also affect the supply of government debt.
views.keep_wondering: How much reflects policy expectations versus debt supply?

views.body: Bond dealers connect buyers and sellers while managing inventory. Fast yield changes can widen the gap between buying and selling prices.

headline: Google signed a 20-year nuclear power deal
commentary: Google and Constellation Energy announced a 20-year power purchase agreement. The deal covers nuclear upgrades in the PJM regional grid. Data centers can link computing, power plants, building work, and grid plans.

defines.used_by_and_why: Predictable demand for a producer; planned supply for a buyer.

explains.anchor_text: connect computing investment with power generation, construction, and grid planning
explains.why: Data centers use electricity, so added computing capacity can require generation and transmission investment.
explains.other_reading: Timing, regulation, demand, and construction costs can change the result.

visual.title: Planned project figures
visual.caption: Planned project figures, per company filings.
visual.alt: Planned reactor upgrades include 890 megawatts of capacity, more than 4.3 billion dollars of investment, and about 7,200 construction jobs.

views.body: Household electricity rates reflect grid investment, regulation, and regional demand. The project plans added supply without direct residential investment costs.
views.keep_wondering: When could the added supply enter the grid?

views.body: A long contract can give a power producer predictable demand. The buyer gains a planned source of electricity for future operations.
views.keep_wondering: How will construction timing affect delivery?

views.body: Regulators oversee reactor upgrades and regional grid planning. Construction timing and approvals can affect when capacity becomes available.

data_note: Capacity and job figures describe plans, not completed work.

headline: Large U.S. companies begin reporting profits
commentary: Corporate earnings reports from large U.S. companies begin over the coming days. A stock is a claim on future company profits. Interest rates can influence stock prices relative to those profits.

defines.used_by_and_why: Used to compare stock prices with business performance.

explains.anchor_text: Interest rates can influence stock prices relative to those profits
explains.why: Investors compare future profits with returns available from bonds.
explains.other_reading: Reported earnings can outweigh interest-rate changes.

visual.title: Reporting begins
visual.fact_text: Delta Air Lines, then major banks
visual.caption: Companies begin reporting over the coming days.
visual.alt: Delta Air Lines reports first, followed by major banks.

views.body: Retirement accounts can change with broad stock indexes. Company profits do not guarantee matching gains in wages or household buying power.
views.keep_wondering: Are gains spread across many companies?

views.body: Market makers quote prices as earnings releases add new information. Uncertainty can widen the gap between buying and selling prices.
views.keep_wondering: How do prices change after each report?

data_note: Company reports contain results; analyst estimates are expectations.
